region.text: Moesia and Thrace from Marcianople to the Utus, Thermopylae and the Chersonese

ledger.note: 447: Attila's second Balkan war. 'In 447, Attila again rode south into the Eastern Roman Empire through Moesia' (Attila page); 'Marcianople fell immediately to the Huns, who destroyed it'; the Roman field armies 'were annihilated' on the Utus; he 'rampaged through the Balkans as far as Thermopylae' and 'defeated a second Roman army in the Chersonesus'.

region.text: Moesia and Thrace; the buffer strip from Singidunum to Novae

ledger.note: 449: the war ends. The Huns page has 'In 449 the East Romans agreed to pay Attila an annual tribute of 2100 pounds of gold'; the Battle of the Utus page has the treaty 'in the fall of 447 or a year later in 448': 6,000 pounds of gold up front and 2,100 a year, and a no man's land 'from Singidunum to Novae' 'with a depth of 100 miles or five days' journey south of the Danube', a buffer inside Roman territory. The year moved from 448 to 449 (the Huns page and eastern-roman-empire's contest_end); the Utus page's 447/448 treaty is the same settlement. The ledger transfers nothing; the strip is the contest zone until the peace (eastern-roman-empire records it as a loss in 447 and gains in 451 and 455: for eu-05).

union.text: the ceded Pannonian land, direct Hun land from 433

region.text: the belt of Germanic subject lands north of the Danube that Cliopatria's 451 and 452 Hun shapes add to the 443 outline: Germany east of the Rhine, Bohemia, Slovakia and Poland up to 53.7 N (about 2,400 cells), without Gaul, northern Italy and Pannonia

ledger.note: 451: Attila gathers his vassals; the Germanic belt is drawn as a vassal region. 'Attila gathered his vassals - Gepids, Ostrogoths, Rugians, Scirians, Heruls, Thuringians' for the march on Gaul (Attila page: 'many retained their own identities and rulers but acknowledged the suzerainty of the king of the Huns'; 'The Huns dominated a vast territory with nebulous borders'). The Huns page lists 'Goths, Gepids, Sarmatians, Heruli, Alans, Rugii, Suevi, and Sciri' among those ruled and says it is 'generally assumed' the empire reached the Rhine, while Maenchen-Helfen and Golden think Attila 'probably controlled only Pannonia and nearby areas'. No page bounds the belt or dates its subjection (Attila reigned 434-453); 451 is the year Cliopatria draws it and the year the page shows the vassals in the field; the extent is Cliopatria's outline (confidence 1). The Gepid and Ostrogothic parts that Cliopatria draws inside the 443 outline are direct land in this dossier.

region.text: Gaul between the Rhine and the Loire: Metz, Reims, Troyes, Orléans

ledger.note: 451: Attila invades Gaul. He 'crossed the Rhine early in 451 with his followers and a large number of allies', sacked Metz on 7 April, passed Reims and Troyes and besieged Orléans, launching 'his final assault on 14 June', broken off as Aetius and Theodoric approached. A campaign zone, hatched (rule 4); Cliopatria draws Gaul as Hun land for 451.

region.text: Gaul between the Rhine and the Loire

ledger.note: 20 June 451: the Catalaunian Plains. The battle 'circa 20 June' near Châlons or Troyes was 'inconclusive' in the contemporary sources and fought 'when he was in full retreat' (Bury); Attila 'withdrew to his homeland'.

region.text: Aquileia and the Po Valley to the Mincio

ledger.note: 452: Attila in Italy. 'a 3-month siege of Aquileia' (Catalaunian Plains page), which he 'razed so completely that it was afterwards hard to recognize its original site', then the Po Valley; Pope Leo I met him 'at Mincio in the vicinity of Mantua'. Hatched campaign zone; Cliopatria draws northern Italy as Hun land 452-454.

region.text: Aquileia and the Po Valley

ledger.note: 452: Attila 'withdrew from Italy to his palace across the Danube', 'most likely because of famine and disease in his army' (Catalaunian Plains page). He 'died in the early months of 453'.

region.text: Dacia, the Gepids' share: 'ruled as victors over the extent of all Dacia' (Jordanes, Gepids page); the Rugii, Heruli, Sciri and Suebi are to the north-west

ledger.note: 454: Nedao; the Germanic subjects break free. Ardaric's Gepids with the Heruli, Rugii, Sciri and Suebi defeated the Huns 'in Pannonia' in 454 ('Germanic victory; End of the Huns rule in Eastern Europe', Battle of Nedao page; the Gepids page has '454 or 455'); 'by the early 460s the Hunnic Empire dissolved' with the Gepids, Rugii, Heruli, Suebi and Ostrogoths 'achieving independence'. The Gepid kingdom 'covered a large part of the former Roman province of Dacia, north of the Danube' (Gepids page, which does not name the Banat, Oltenia, Wallachia or Moldavia). The region is the named parts of Dacia that Cliopatria's 455 Hun shape drops; Oltenia was added in review. Cliopatria has no Gepid row before 510 (notes): the counterpart is the Gepids of 454-509.

union.text: the ceded Pannonian land, direct Hun land from 433

region.text: the belt of Germanic subject lands north of the Danube that Cliopatria's 451 and 452 Hun shapes add to the 443 outline: Germany east of the Rhine, Bohemia, Slovakia and Poland up to 53.7 N (about 2,400 cells), without Gaul, northern Italy and Pannonia

ledger.note: 454: Nedao ends the Hun suzerainty. 'Ardaric led a Germanic coalition to overthrow Hunnic imperial authority' and, after Attila's death, 'the Huns were driven out of Pannonia' (Huns page); the Battle of Nedao page has 'Germanic victory; End of the Huns rule in Eastern Europe' and the Gepids, Rugii, Heruli, Sciri and Suebi among the victors. The belt passes to no state of record: the Rugii (Rugiland, 455), the Thuringians (Thuringian states, 469) and the Danubian Suebi have rows or dossiers only later or elsewhere.

region.text: the Danube-Tisza interfluve, the Bacska and the middle and upper Tisza

ledger.note: 454: the Pannonian plain passes to the Gepids. The Gepids page has their population 'mostly centred on the Someş and Körös rivers' and the kingdom 'centered on Sirmium' (after 473); it does not name the Danube-Tisza interfluve. Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Gepids shape (510) covers 199 of these 323 cells. Confidence 1: the plain is the cells Cliopatria's Hun shape drops in 455, ledger 407 is its mirror.

region.text: Pannonia, the Ostrogoths' settlement: the Hungarian cells of the Western Roman Empire's 426 shape that the Huns held from 433

ledger.note: 455: Pannonia passes to the Ostrogoths. The Ostrogoths page has their freedom from Attila's sons 'confirmed by the Battle of Nedao in 454', Valamir 'r. 447-c. 465', and the Amal-led Goths 'apparently first settled in the Pannonian area of Lake Balaton and Sirmium' (no date); the Huns page: 'The Huns were driven out of Pannonia, and some returned to the Pontic Steppe'. The year is Cliopatria's Ostrogoths row (455); the Ostrogoths page, opened in review, does not date the settlement, so the confidence stays 1.

region.text: Moldavia, Bessarabia, Bukovina, Maramures and eastern Galicia, the western margins of the steppe shape that Cliopatria's 455 Hun shape (22.6 E eastward) no longer covers

ledger.note: 455: the western margins leave the Hun shape. 'The Huns were driven out of Pannonia, and some returned to the Pontic Steppe' (Huns page); Cliopatria's 455 shape holds the steppe east of about 22.6 E and drops Moldavia, Bessarabia, Bukovina and the Carpathian arc (about 500 cells, 130,000 km2) that its 443-454 shape held. No page names a state there (the Gepids' Dacia is ledger 454); the cells are stateless from 455 (confidence 1).

region.text: Thrace and the lower Danube, where Dengizich 'threatened Thrace unless he received land and subsidies'

ledger.note: 467: Dengizich crosses the Danube. After the Romans refused 'a market place on the Danube' (465-466) and Leo I demanded obedience, 'In 467, Dengizich crossed the frozen Danube'; 'the war dragged on for about two years'; c. 468 he 'beleaguered' Bassianae in Pannonia and 'began to plunder its territory' until the Goths drove the Huns out.

region.text: Thrace and the lower Danube

ledger.note: 469: Dengizich killed. Marcellinus Comes: 'The head of Dinzic, son of Attila, king of the Huns, was brought to Constantinople'; the Chronicon Paschale credits Anagastes, the Thracian general, and says the head was displayed in the city.

region.text: the Pontic steppe between the Carpathians and the Volga, the Huns' last land of record

ledger.note: 469: the Hun state ends. 'In 469, Dengizich was defeated and killed in Thrace'; 'After that point, the Huns cease to exist in European history.' Ernak's Huns remain settlers in Scythia Minor under Rome ('The fate of Ernak is unclear', Ernak page); the Pontic steppe passes to no state of record (Cliopatria's Old Great Bulgaria begins 633); Cliopatria's residual shapes 469-673 are dropped (keyframe_review).

wars.name: Hunnic conquest of the Alans and Goths

zones.text: from the Don to the Dniester and the Carpathians

wars.outcome: The Alans of the Don submitted c. 370; Ermanaric's Greuthungi fell in 375-376 (his suicide, Vithimiris' death); the Thervingi crossed the Danube in 376 and Athanaric's remnant fled to Caucaland. The Pontic steppe and the plains north of the Danube became Hun land.
wars.note: The Balamber page warns that the Hun 'king' of Jordanes' account 'may have never existed'; the dates are Ammianus' and the Goths page's.

wars.name: Hun raid of 395

zones.text: Armenia, Cappadocia, northern Syria to Antioch and Euphratesia

wars.outcome: A raid: Armenia overrun, Cappadocia pillaged, Antioch threatened; the simultaneous invasion of the Sasanian Empire 'defeated badly during the Persian counterattack'. No land held; Eutropius' ascension to power 'was assisted by his defeat of a Hun invasion in 398' (Eutropius (consul 399) page), which closes the raid.

wars.name: Uldin's invasion of Thrace

zones.text: Castra Martis in Dacia Ripensis and the Thracian diocese

wars.outcome: Castra Martis taken in summer 408; after heavy losses and the Sciri's defection Uldin re-crossed the Danube by 23 March 409. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Hunnic war of 441-443 (first Balkan campaign)

zones.text: Margus, Viminacium, Singidunum, Sirmium, Ratiaria, Naissus

wars.outcome: The Danube cities of Illyricum sacked in 441 and Ratiaria and Naissus in 443; the Peace of Anatolius (autumn 443) tripled the tribute to 2,100 Roman pounds a year. No annexation.

wars.name: Attila's campaign of 447 and the Battle of the Utus

zones.text: Marcianople, the Utus, the Balkans to Thermopylae, the Chersonese

wars.outcome: Hunnic victory; peace in the fall of 447 or in 448 (the Huns page: the tribute agreed in 449): 6,000 pounds of gold up front, 2,100 a year, and a buffer 'five days' journey' deep from Singidunum to Novae left as no man's land inside Roman territory.
wars.note: The buffer strip is drawn as a contest blend for 447-448 and then left Roman; the pages do not say when the Romans reoccupied it. The war ends 449 here (Huns page; eastern-roman-empire has 449), the Utus page's 447/448 being the same treaty.

wars.name: Attila's invasion of Gaul

zones.text: Gaul from the Rhine to Orléans

wars.outcome: Metz sacked 7 April, Orléans besieged to 14 June, the Catalaunian Plains c. 20 June 'inconclusive' and fought during Attila's retreat; Theodoric I killed; Attila 'withdrew to his homeland'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The Kingdom of the Burgundians page: 'In 451, the Burgundians helped the Roman-led allies defeat Attila'. Cliopatria's 451 Hun shape includes Gaul; the keyframe removes it.

wars.name: Attila's invasion of Italy

zones.text: Aquileia and the Po Valley to the Mincio

wars.outcome: Aquileia razed after a three-month siege, the Po Valley ravaged, Pope Leo's embassy at the Mincio; Attila withdrew across the Danube, most likely for famine and disease. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: 'Germanic victory; End of the Huns rule in Eastern Europe'; 'by the early 460s the Hunnic Empire dissolved' with the Gepids, Rugii, Heruli, Suebi and Ostrogoths independent, later Eastern Roman federates; the Huns under Dengizich moved east to the Pontic steppe.
wars.note: The Gepids, Heruli, Rugii, Sciri and Danubian Suebi have no Cliopatria rows in 454 (Rugiland and Ostrogoths begin 455); part c adds them.

wars.name: Dengizich's war on the Danube

zones.text: Bassianae in Pannonia, besieged c. 468 against the Ostrogoths

wars.outcome: Dengizich crossed the frozen Danube in 467, besieged Bassianae c. 468 and was driven off by the Goths; killed in Thrace in 469, his head displayed in Constantinople. The Hun state ends.

certainty.note: A steppe people with no recorded border; the Caspian shape is Cliopatria's placement of 'east of the Volga'.
Steppe and Carpathian-basin frontiers throughout; the Danube is the one sharp line, with the Roman provinces, and the 433 Pannonian cession follows Roman provincial limits.

notes:
Rows merged: Cliopatria's 'Huns' (106-425) and 'Hunnic Empire' (426-673) share Wikidata Q45813 and are one polity: Octar and Rugila (c. 420s-430), Rugila (430-435) and Bleda and Attila (434/435-) rule the same confederation across the 426 boundary, and colours.json already groups both slugs under 'huns'. This dossier reviews both rows' shapes under the earlier slug 'huns'. hunnic-empire is listed as a sibling part's polity in the brief: part b should not write hunnic-empire.json, or the orchestrator must drop one of the two (reported under problems).

Start and end: the start year 106 is Cliopatria's; the Huns page says only that they were 'first reported living east of the Volga' and 'appeared in Europe suddenly around 370' (found event at confidence 1). The state ends in 469 with Dengizich's death ('the Huns cease to exist in European history'); the four residual shapes 469-673 (185 km2 and 46 km2) are marked wrong and dropped.

Cliopatria shapes corrected: 373 is two to three years early for the Gothic lands (375-376); 396-406 carry Cappadocia and northern Syria south to 35.9 N, which is the raid of 395 drawn as territory for ten years; 443-450 dips into Roman Moesia and Thrace; 451 includes Gaul and 452-454 northern Italy, both campaigns; the ceded Pannonian land of 433 is missing from the 'Hunnic Empire' shapes (western edge 18.7 E). The reach of the 451-454 shapes to the Rhine, the North Sea and the Baltic is the belt of Germanic subject peoples: since the repair of review eu-06-a it is a vassal region (ledger 451-454, counterpart "Attila's Germanic vassal peoples"), not direct land.

Counterparts that need dossiers (another group or part c): the Alans of the Don and Kuban are now covered by the sarmatians dossier (the 370 gain names it); the Gepids of 454-509 (Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Gepids row begins 510; the 454 loss names kingdom-of-the-gepids); the Rugii, Heruli, Sciri and Danubian Suebi of 454; the Akatziri. 

Vassal relations the suzerain dossiers should carry: none for the Huns as suzerain beyond the Germanic belt; Ernak's Huns in Scythia Minor after 454 are Eastern Roman settlers (eastern-roman-empire).

The page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eutropius_(consul) would not load; review eu-06-a opened https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eutropius_(consul_399), which dates the defeat of the Hun invasion to 398, and moved the occupation_end from 396 (confidence 1) to 398 (confidence 2). Disagreements between pages: Attila's accession 434 (Attila and Bleda infoboxes) or 435 (Attila lead, Huns infobox); Rugila's death 434 (Chronica Gallica) or 435; the Pannonian cession 425, 431 or 433; the 447/448 peace year.

Gazetteer: 'Pannonia' is not in regions.jsonl; since the repair the dossier uses the explicit region of western-roman-empire ledger 21 (the Hungarian cells of the Western Roman Empire's 426 shape) for the 433 cession, the keyframes and the 455 loss, so that it resolves without warnings. The capital dot for Attila's court is a convention on the Tisza plain; the pages give no site.

Repair of review eu-06-a (2026-10-19). (1) 398: occupation_end moved from 396 to 398 by the review (Eutropius page); the war entry was aligned. (2) Belt of Germanic subject lands: the 451-454 keyframes now describe direct land only (the 443 outline with Pannonia, without Gaul, northern Italy and the belt); the belt is a vassal region 451-454 with a composite counterpart because Cliopatria and the pages give no state for it (Attila page: vassals 'Gepids, Ostrogoths, Rugians, Scirians, Heruls, Thuringians'; Huns page: the Rhine is 'generally assumed', two scholars hold Attila 'probably controlled only Pannonia and nearby areas'). Confidence 1 on the extent. (3) 373-375: the correction of huns_373 is now exactly the 373 shape minus Gothia 372 for 373-374, with new keyframes huns_372 (Bosporan Kingdom), huns_375 (Greuthungi steppe) and huns_376 (Thervingi plains); new gains: 372 from cimmerian-bosporus (Chersonesus page: captured by the Huns 'in the 370s', year Cliopatria's, confidence 1) and 373 from the sarmatians for 537 cells of steppe (confidence 1, no page dates it). (4) huns_378 is adjusted to the union of the Hun shape and Gothia 373 (692 cells that Cliopatria adds only in 383); gothia keyframe 12 can now say the Huns hold them. (5) The 325 cells added in 407 are a gain from the Iazyges (sarmatians) in 407 at confidence 1 and leave to the Gepids in 454; the Pontic-Danubian margins that Cliopatria's 455 shape drops leave to nobody in 455 (about 500 cells, confidence 1). The Sarmatians page dates the Alan conquest 375 and the sarmatians dossier dissolves the Iazyges at 375; this dossier keeps 370 for the Alans (Alans and Huns pages) and 407 for the Iazyges (the Iazyges page has only 'by the time of Attila'): a mismatch for the orchestrator. (6) hunnic-empire_426 now keeps Cliopatria's shape for 426-432 and the new keyframe hunnic-empire_433 adds Pannonia, as the page dates the cession. (7) Counterparts: ledger 1 names sarmatians. Ledger 17 names kingdom-of-the-gepids as before: no gepids dossier exists yet and the orchestrator has assigned no slug; when one is assigned, ledger 17, 454 and the successor entry should use it. (8) contest_end of the war of 447 moved from 448 to 449 (Huns page, and eastern-roman-empire has 449). Disagreement kept: eastern-roman-empire records losses of the Danube cities (441), the Singidunum-Novae strip (447) and gains (451, 455); the Huns page has only a truce in 441, the Peace of Anatolius in 443 and the strip as 'a no man's land in the Roman territory' (Utus page), so this dossier keeps contest zones and the eastern-roman-empire side is the one to change (eu-05). (9) Rulers: the strip has gaps 380-399 and 410-411 because the pages opened name no ruler; the rulers' notes say so. (10) Thin: found 106 stays at confidence 1 (the Xiongnu page does not date the Huns on the Volga); the 455 Ostrogothic settlement stays at confidence 1 (the Ostrogoths page gives no date). (11) Area check: neither the Huns nor the Attila page has an infobox area (the Huns map caption reads 'Estimated territory under Hunnic political control under Attila, c. 450 CE', no figure), so the factor-of-two comparison is impossible; Cliopatria's peak is 1.91 M km2 (451), 1.81 M (452), of which the belt of the Germanic subjects is about 0.6 M and Gaul and northern Italy about 0.2 M, and the corrected direct land is about 1.25 M km2 (the 443 outline) at its largest. Residuals that the repair accepts: the 443-454 outline still carries about 20 cells of western Bulgaria (23-24 E) that the Moesia-Thrace subtraction does not cover; the Kerch core (26 cells) is in the 372 gain although cimmerian-bosporus ledger 23 leaves it with the Bosporan Kingdom; the keyframes huns_396 and huns_397 (not in the review's findings) keep 30 cells of north-west Iran (44-45 E, 38.4-39.7 N) that no event or region subtraction covers; the one-year overlap with gothia (its keyframe keeps the Greuthungi steppe through 375, the Huns hold it from 375).
